reasoning: Impurity has risen from 22 ppm at 04:55 to 38 ppm at 05:10 — a rate of >5 ppm/min — while pH remains flat at 7.14 and the temperature reading is still at 33.0°C tracking setpoint exactly. This is the run_003 sensor-lag signature: impurity is responding to an actual thermal event in solution that the temperature probe has not yet detected due to its 2-3 minute thermal mass lag. Raising setpoint by +0.5°C to preempt the dip the probe will likely report shortly. Small step only — run_003 showed that overcorrection (>0.5°C) compounds the thermal shock. pH stability rules out chemical contamination as the cause.
outcome: Temperature reading dropped to 32.4°C at 05:20 UTC — confirming the thermal event 3 minutes after the intervention had already been applied. Impurity peaked at 42 ppm at 05:15 and began falling immediately. By 05:25 impurity was back below the 35 ppm warning threshold (34 ppm). By 05:30 temperature recovered to 33.3°C. Setpoint returned to planned 33.0°C trajectory at 05:40.

reasoning: pH has risen monotonically from 7.10 at run start to 7.30 at 07:05 — a drift of +0.20 units over 5 hours with zero direction reversals. Rate is ~0.04/hour, distinct from typical probe noise (~0.05/hour oscillating). This is real solution chemistry and matches the run_004 drift signature exactly: same substrate (KDP), same monotonic direction, comparable rate. No individual reading has crossed the 7.4 warning threshold and the system would not fire a threshold-based alert — but run_004 demonstrated that this exact pattern reaches the 7.6 hydrolysis threshold within ~1.5 hours when left alone. Preemptive 3 ml buffer addition (the policy minimum from remediation.contamination_suspected.start_volume_ml) is cheap reversible insurance against an irreversible hydrolysis event.
outcome: pH stopped climbing immediately. Peak held at 7.30 across 07:05 and 07:10 readings, then began declining: 7.29 at 07:15, 7.27 at 07:20, 7.26 at 07:25, 7.25 at 07:30. The monotonic drift was broken — three consecutive readings showed stable or declining pH. No further intervention required. pH stabilized at 7.25–7.30 range for the remaining 2.5 hours of the run.
